```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

project_folder <- "/Users/purnagamage/Documents/GitHub/DS-Corps-Assessents"

folder <- file.path(
  project_folder,
  "all_variables_needed"
)

week4_folder <- file.path(
  project_folder,
  "Week_4"
)

dir.create(
  week4_folder,
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

files <- c(
  "AI_historical_data.csv",
  "GOOGL_historical_data.csv",
  "MSFT_historical_data.csv",
  "NVDA_historical_data.csv",
  "all_capex_ppi_daily_interpolated.csv",
  "GT_jobs_int.csv",
  "GT_skills_int.csv",
  "indeed_data_analysis.csv",
  "indeed-all.csv",
  "indeed-software.csv"
)

read_file <- function(filename) {

  data <- read_csv(
    file.path(folder, filename),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  # Find the date column
  date_col <- names(data)[
    grepl("date|month|time", names(data), ignore.case = TRUE)
  ][1]

  if (is.na(date_col)) {
    stop("No date column found in: ", filename)
  }

  # Convert the date
  date_values <- as.character(data[[date_col]])

  parsed_dates <- suppressWarnings(
    as.Date(
      parse_date_time(
        date_values,
        orders = c(
          "ymd",
          "mdy",
          "dmy",
          "ym",
          "my",
          "Ymd",
          "bY",
          "BY",
          "bdy",
          "Ymd HMS",
          "ymd HMS"
        )
      )
    )
  )

  if (all(is.na(parsed_dates))) {
    stop(
      "Dates could not be read in: ",
      filename,
      "\nFirst date values: ",
      paste(head(date_values), collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  # Rename the date column
  names(data)[names(data) == date_col] <- "Date"
  data$Date <- parsed_dates

  # Remove rows with missing dates
  data <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(Date))

  # Add filename to the other column names
  file_name <- make.names(
    tools::file_path_sans_ext(filename)
  )

  data %>%
    rename_with(
      ~ paste0(file_name, "_", .x),
      -Date
    )
}

# Load the files
data_list <- lapply(files, read_file)

# Find the common overlapping period
common_start <- as.Date(
  max(sapply(data_list, function(x) as.numeric(min(x$Date)))),
  origin = "1970-01-01"
)

common_end <- as.Date(
  min(sapply(data_list, function(x) as.numeric(max(x$Date)))),
  origin = "1970-01-01"
)

# Combine all datasets by date
combined_data <- reduce(
  data_list,
  full_join,
  by = "Date"
) %>%
  filter(
    Date >= common_start,
    Date <= common_end
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)

# Check the result
range(combined_data$Date)
dim(combined_data)
```

```{r}
# Maximum CCF lag in days
lag_max <- 30

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Functions for selecting columns
# ------------------------------------------------------------

get_numeric_columns <- function(pattern) {
  
  columns <- grep(
    pattern,
    names(combined_data),
    value = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
  
  if (length(columns) == 0) {
    return(character(0))
  }
  
  numeric_columns <- vapply(
    columns,
    function(column_name) {
      is.numeric(combined_data[[column_name]])
    },
    logical(1)
  )
  
  return(columns[numeric_columns])
}


get_job_column <- function(pattern) {
  
  columns <- get_numeric_columns(pattern)
  
  if (length(columns) == 0) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  
  preferred <- columns[
    grepl(
      "main[._]?value|job.*opening|posting.*index|value",
      columns,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )
  ]
  
  if (length(preferred) > 0) {
    return(preferred[1])
  }
  
  return(columns[1])
}


get_stock_column <- function(pattern) {
  
  columns <- get_numeric_columns(pattern)
  
  if (length(columns) == 0) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  
  # Prefer adjusted closing price
  preferred <- columns[
    grepl(
      "adj.*close|adjusted.*close",
      columns,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )
  ]
  
  # Otherwise use another closing-price column
  if (length(preferred) == 0) {
    preferred <- columns[
      grepl(
        "close",
        columns,
        ignore.case = TRUE
      )
    ]
  }
  
  if (length(preferred) > 0) {
    return(preferred[1])
  }
  
  return(columns[1])
}
```

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Create one regularly spaced daily dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

needed_columns <- unique(
  c(
    "Date",
    unname(job_columns),
    unname(predictor_columns)
  )
)

ccf_data <- combined_data[
  ,
  needed_columns,
  drop = FALSE
]

ccf_data$Date <- as.Date(ccf_data$Date)

# Average duplicate dates, if there are any
ccf_data <- aggregate(
  ccf_data[, -1, drop = FALSE],
  by = list(Date = ccf_data$Date),
  FUN = function(x) {
    if (all(is.na(x))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
)

# Create a complete daily date sequence
daily_dates <- data.frame(
  Date = seq(
    min(ccf_data$Date),
    max(ccf_data$Date),
    by = "day"
  )
)

ccf_data <- merge(
  daily_dates,
  ccf_data,
  by = "Date",
  all.x = TRUE
)

ccf_data <- ccf_data[
  order(ccf_data$Date),
]

# Interpolate missing internal daily values
interpolate_daily <- function(x, dates) {
  
  available <- !is.na(x)
  
  if (sum(available) < 2) {
    return(x)
  }
  
  approx(
    x = as.numeric(dates[available]),
    y = x[available],
    xout = as.numeric(dates),
    rule = 1
  )$y
}

for (column in setdiff(names(ccf_data), "Date")) {
  
  ccf_data[[column]] <- interpolate_daily(
    ccf_data[[column]],
    ccf_data$Date
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Calculate all CCF values and create all CCF plots
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ccf_results <- list()
result_number <- 1

pdf(
  file.path(week4_folder, "CCF_all_plots.pdf"),
  width = 10,
  height = 7
)

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {
  
  job_column <- job_columns[[job_name]]
  
  for (predictor_name in names(predictor_columns)) {
    
    predictor_column <- predictor_columns[[predictor_name]]
    
    pair_data <- ccf_data[
      complete.cases(
        ccf_data[, c(job_column, predictor_column)]
      ),
      c(job_column, predictor_column),
      drop = FALSE
    ]
    
    job_values <- pair_data[[job_column]]
    predictor_values <- pair_data[[predictor_column]]
    
    if (
      length(job_values) > lag_max + 2 &&
      sd(job_values) > 0 &&
      sd(predictor_values) > 0
    ) {
      
      ccf_object <- ccf(
        job_values,
        predictor_values,
        lag.max = lag_max,
        plot = TRUE,
        main = paste(
          job_name,
          "Job Openings vs",
          predictor_name
        ),
        xlab = "Lag in days"
      )
      
      ccf_results[[result_number]] <- data.frame(
        Category = predictor_groups[[predictor_name]],
        Job_Openings = job_name,
        Predictor = predictor_name,
        Lag = as.numeric(ccf_object$lag),
        CCF = as.numeric(ccf_object$acf),
        N = length(job_values),
        Approx_95_Bound = 1.96 / sqrt(length(job_values))
      )
      
      result_number <- result_number + 1
    }
  }
}

dev.off()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Combine all CCF values into one table
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ccf_values <- do.call(
  rbind,
  ccf_results
)

ccf_values$Significant <- abs(ccf_values$CCF) >
  ccf_values$Approx_95_Bound

# Find the strongest absolute CCF for each comparison
comparison_groups <- interaction(
  ccf_values$Job_Openings,
  ccf_values$Predictor,
  drop = TRUE
)

ccf_peak_values <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    split(ccf_values, comparison_groups),
    function(x) {
      x[which.max(abs(x$CCF)), ]
    }
  )
)

rownames(ccf_peak_values) <- NULL

# Interpretation of the lag direction
ccf_peak_values$Lag_Interpretation <- ifelse(
  ccf_peak_values$Lag > 0,
  "Predictor leads job openings",
  ifelse(
    ccf_peak_values$Lag < 0,
    "Job openings lead predictor",
    "Same-day relationship"
  )
)

# Sort the peak results
ccf_peak_values <- ccf_peak_values[
  order(
    ccf_peak_values$Category,
    ccf_peak_values$Job_Openings,
    -abs(ccf_peak_values$CCF)
  ),
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Save and view the results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

write.csv(
  ccf_values,
  file.path(week4_folder, "CCF_all_values.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  ccf_peak_values,
  file.path(week4_folder, "CCF_peak_values.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare Google Trends CCF results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

google_ccf <- ccf_values %>%
  filter(Category == "Google Trends") %>%
  mutate(
    Job_Type = recode(
      Job_Openings,
      "DA"  = "Data Analysis",
      "SW"  = "Software Development",
      "ALL" = "All Job Openings",
      .default = Job_Openings
    ),
    
    Trend_Type = ifelse(
      grepl("GT Job", Predictor),
      "Job-title search",
      "Skill search"
    ),
    
    Search_Term = Predictor %>%
      sub("^GT Job: ", "", .) %>%
      sub("^GT Skill: ", "", .) %>%
      gsub("_", " ", .) %>%
      gsub("\\.", " ", .)
  )

# Create approximate 95% bounds if they are not already present
if (!"Approx_95_Bound" %in% names(google_ccf)) {
  google_ccf <- google_ccf %>%
    mutate(Approx_95_Bound = 1.96 / sqrt(N))
}
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Main project folder
project_folder <- "/Users/purnagamage/Documents/GitHub/DS-Corps-Assessents"

# Folder for saving Google Trends CCF plots
plot_folder <- file.path(
  project_folder,
  "Week_4",
  "CCF_Google_Trends_Plots"
)

dir.create(
  plot_folder,
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

# Job-opening categories
job_types <- unique(google_ccf$Job_Type)

for (job in job_types) {

  plot_data <- google_ccf %>%
    filter(Job_Type == job)

  confidence_bounds <- plot_data %>%
    distinct(
      Search_Term,
      Approx_95_Bound
    )

  ccf_plot <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(x = Lag, y = CCF)
  ) +

    # Zero line
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = 0,
      linewidth = 0.4
    ) +

    # Confidence limits
    geom_hline(
      data = confidence_bounds,
      aes(yintercept = Approx_95_Bound),
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = 0.5,
      color = "steelblue"
    ) +

    geom_hline(
      data = confidence_bounds,
      aes(yintercept = -Approx_95_Bound),
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = 0.5,
      color = "steelblue"
    ) +

    # CCF lines
    geom_segment(
      aes(
        xend = Lag,
        y = 0,
        yend = CCF
      ),
      linewidth = 0.5,
      color = "gray35"
    ) +

    facet_wrap(
      ~ Search_Term,
      ncol = 3
    ) +

    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = seq(
        min(plot_data$Lag),
        max(plot_data$Lag),
        by = 10
      )
    ) +

    labs(
      title = paste(
        "Cross-Correlation:",
        job,
        "vs Google Search Interest"
      ),
      subtitle = paste(
        "Positive lags indicate that Google search interest",
        "leads job openings"
      ),
      x = "Lag in days",
      y = "Cross-correlation coefficient",
      caption = "Dashed lines show approximate 95% confidence limits."
    ) +

    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 17
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 11
      ),
      strip.text = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 10
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines"),
      plot.caption = element_text(
        hjust = 0,
        face = "italic"
      )
    )

  # Display the plot
  print(ccf_plot)

  # Create a safe filename
  file_name <- paste0(
    "CCF_",
    gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", job),
    "_vs_Google_Trends.png"
  )

  # Save the plot
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(plot_folder, file_name),
    plot = ccf_plot,
    width = 13,
    height = 9,
    dpi = 300
  )
}
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

all_heatmap_data <- ccf_values %>%
  mutate(
    Job_Type = recode(
      Job_Openings,
      "DA"  = "Data Analysis",
      "SW"  = "Software Development",
      "ALL" = "All Job Openings",
      .default = Job_Openings
    ),

    # Set the order of the three heatmap sections
    Category = factor(
      as.character(Category),
      levels = c(
        "Google Trends",
        "Stock Prices",
        "CAPEX and PPI"
      )
    ),

    Predictor_Label = case_when(
      grepl("PCU", Predictor, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "PPI",
      grepl("CAPEX", Predictor, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "CAPEX",
      TRUE ~ Predictor
    ),

    Predictor_Label = Predictor_Label %>%
      gsub("^GT Job: ", "Google Trends—Job Title: ", .) %>%
      gsub("^GT Skill: ", "Google Trends—Skill: ", .) %>%
      gsub("_", " ", .) %>%
      gsub("\\.", " ", .),

    Comparison = paste(
      Job_Type,
      Predictor_Label,
      sep = " — "
    )
  )

# Arrange rows using the new category order
comparison_order <- all_heatmap_data %>%
  distinct(
    Category,
    Job_Type,
    Predictor_Label,
    Comparison
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    Category,
    Job_Type,
    Predictor_Label
  ) %>%
  pull(Comparison)

all_heatmap_data$Comparison <- factor(
  all_heatmap_data$Comparison,
  levels = rev(comparison_order)
)
```

```{r}
  filter(Category == "Stock Prices") %>%
  mutate(
    Job_Type = recode(
      Job_Openings,
      "ALL" = "All Job Openings",
      "DA"  = "Data Analysis",
      "SW"  = "Software Development",
      .default = Job_Openings
    ),

    Stock = recode(
      Predictor,
      "C3AI"  = "C3.ai",
      "GOOGL" = "Alphabet (GOOGL)",
      "MSFT"  = "Microsoft (MSFT)",
      "NVDA"  = "NVIDIA (NVDA)",
      .default = Predictor
    ),

    Direction = ifelse(
      CCF >= 0,
      "Positive",
      "Negative"
    ),

    Job_Type = factor(
      Job_Type,
      levels = c(
        "All Job Openings",
        "Data Analysis",
        "Software Development"
      )
    ),

    Stock = factor(
      Stock,
      levels = c(
        "C3.ai",
        "Alphabet (GOOGL)",
        "Microsoft (MSFT)",
        "NVIDIA (NVDA)"
      )
    )
  )

# Confidence limits for each panel
stock_bounds <- stock_ccf %>%
  distinct(
    Job_Type,
    Stock,
    Approx_95_Bound
  )
```

```{r}
fit_models <- function(predictors) {

    lm(
      reformulate(
        termlabels = unname(predictors),
```

```{r}
model_results <- function(models, model_group) {
  
  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(models), function(job) {
      
      model_summary <- summary(models[[job]])
      
      data.frame(
        Model_Group = model_group,
        Job_Openings = job,
        R_Squared = model_summary$r.squared,
        Adjusted_R_Squared = model_summary$adj.r.squared,
        RMSE = model_summary$sigma,
        AIC = AIC(models[[job]]),
        Observations = nobs(models[[job]])
      )
    })
  )
}

regression_results <- rbind(
  model_results(google_models, "Google Trends"),
  model_results(stock_models, "Stock Prices"),
  model_results(economic_models, "CAPEX and PPI")
)

regression_results
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(broom)


# Function to summarize a list of models
make_model_summary <- function(model_list, model_group) {
  
  bind_rows(lapply(names(model_list), function(x) {
    
    fit <- glance(model_list[[x]])
    
    data.frame(
      Model = model_group,
      Job_Openings = x,
      R_Squared = round(fit$r.squared, 3),
      Adj_R_Squared = round(fit$adj.r.squared, 3),
      RMSE = round(sqrt(mean(residuals(model_list[[x]])^2)), 2),
      N = nobs(model_list[[x]])
    )
  }))
}

# Create one simple summary table
results_table <- bind_rows(
  make_model_summary(google_models, "Google Trends"),
  make_model_summary(stock_models, "Stock Prices"),
  make_model_summary(economic_models, "CAPEX & PPI")
)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create readable labels
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "Data Analysis Job Openings",
  SW  = "Software Development Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

job_lookup <- tibble(
  Column = unname(job_columns),
  Series = unname(job_labels[names(job_columns)])
)

google_lookup <- tibble(
  Column = unname(google_columns),
  Series = names(google_columns)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Series = case_when(
      grepl("GT Job", Series, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
        "Google Trends: Job-Title Searches",

      grepl("GT Skill", Series, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
        "Google Trends: Skill Searches",

      TRUE ~ Series
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Convert the data to long format
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_lookup <- bind_rows(
  job_lookup %>% mutate(Group = "Job Openings"),
  google_lookup %>% mutate(Group = "Google Trends")
)

plot_data <- combined_data %>%
  select(
    Date,
    all_of(plot_lookup$Column)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Date,
    names_to = "Column",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    plot_lookup,
    by = "Column"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value))

# Use the same date range for both sections
date_limits <- range(
  plot_data$Date,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Job-opening panels
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_plot <- plot_data %>%
  filter(Group == "Job Openings") %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x = Date, y = Value)
  ) +

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9,
    color = "#1F77B4"
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Series ~ .,
    scales = "free_y",
    switch = "y"
  ) +

  scale_x_date(
    limits = date_limits,
    date_breaks = "6 months",
    date_labels = "%Y",
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Job Openings",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Daily indices for data analysis, software development, ",
      "and all job openings"
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),

    strip.placement = "outside",

    strip.background = element_blank(),

    strip.text.y.left = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      face = "bold",
      size = 10,
      hjust = 1
    ),

    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(
      color = "gray90",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ),

    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      color = "gray90",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ),

    panel.spacing = grid::unit(
      0.7,
      "lines"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      10, 20, 5, 20
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Google Trends panels
# ------------------------------------------------------------

google_plot <- plot_data %>%
  filter(Group == "Google Trends") %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x = Date, y = Value)
  ) +

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9,
    color = "#D55E00"
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Series ~ .,
    scales = "free_y",
    switch = "y"
  ) +

  scale_x_date(
    limits = date_limits,
    date_breaks = "6 months",
    date_labels = "%Y",
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Google Search Interest",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Search-interest indices for AI-related job titles ",
      "and technical skills"
    ),
    x = "Year",
    y = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),

    strip.placement = "outside",

    strip.background = element_blank(),

    strip.text.y.left = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      face = "bold",
      size = 10,
      hjust = 1
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(
      color = "gray90",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ),

    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      color = "gray90",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ),

    panel.spacing = grid::unit(
      0.7,
      "lines"
    ),

    axis.title.x = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      margin = margin(t = 8)
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      5, 20, 10, 20
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Combine the two sections
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_google_figure <- job_plot / google_plot +
  plot_layout(
    heights = c(3, 2)
  ) +

  plot_annotation(
    title = "Job Openings and Google Search Interest Over Time",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Each panel uses its own vertical scale, while all panels ",
      "share the same time axis"
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 22
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 12
      )
    )
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create readable labels

job_labels <- c(

  MSFT  = "Microsoft (MSFT)",

job_lookup <- tibble(
  Column = unname(job_columns),

plot_lookup <- bind_rows(

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Convert the data to long format

jo_stock_plot_data <- combined_data %>%
  select(
    Date,
    all_of(plot_lookup$Column)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Date,
    names_to = "Column",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    plot_lookup,
    by = "Column"
  ) %>%
```

We use CCF to examine lead–lag dependence between job openings and each external signal. Specifically, we estimate the correlation between job openings at time t and lagged values of Google Trends, stock prices, CAPEX, and PPI. This helps us identify whether any predictors appear to lead job-opening changes and may therefore be useful as exogenous inputs in RNN/LSTM forecasting models.

Important statistical point:

CCF is not simply a correlation between two raw time series. If the series are trending or nonstationary, raw CCF can be misleading because both series may share trend, seasonality, or autocorrelation. So you usually apply CCF after some preprocessing, such as differencing, log-differencing, detrending, seasonal adjustment, or prewhitening.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Maximum lag in days
lag_max <- 30

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. First-difference all variables except Date
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ccf_data_diff <- ccf_data %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      -Date,
      ~ .x - lag(.x)
    )
  ) %>%
  slice(-1)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate and plot CCFs using differenced variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ccf_results <- list()
result_number <- 1

# Folder for saving results
diff_folder <- file.path(
  week4_folder,
  "CCF_First_Difference"
)

dir.create(
  diff_folder,
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

# Open one multipage PDF
pdf(
  file.path(
    diff_folder,
    "CCF_first_difference_all_plots.pdf"
  ),
  width = 10,
  height = 7
)

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {

  job_column <- job_columns[[job_name]]

  for (predictor_name in names(predictor_columns)) {

    predictor_column <- predictor_columns[[predictor_name]]

    # Keep complete observations for this pair
    pair_data <- ccf_data_diff %>%
      select(
        all_of(job_column),
        all_of(predictor_column)
      ) %>%
      drop_na()

    job_values <- pair_data[[job_column]]
    predictor_values <- pair_data[[predictor_column]]

    # Only calculate CCF when enough observations are available
    if (
      length(job_values) > lag_max + 2 &&
      sd(job_values) > 0 &&
      sd(predictor_values) > 0
    ) {

      ccf_object <- ccf(
        job_values,
        predictor_values,
        lag.max = lag_max,
        plot = TRUE,
        main = paste(
          "First-Difference CCF:",
          job_name,
          "Job Openings vs",
          predictor_name
        ),
        xlab = "Lag in days",
        ylab = "Cross-correlation"
      )

      ccf_results[[result_number]] <- data.frame(
        Category = predictor_groups[[predictor_name]],
        Job_Openings = job_name,
        Predictor = predictor_name,
        Lag = as.numeric(ccf_object$lag),
        CCF = as.numeric(ccf_object$acf),
        N = length(job_values),
        Approx_95_Bound = 1.96 / sqrt(length(job_values))
      )

      result_number <- result_number + 1
    }
  }
}

dev.off()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Combine and save the CCF results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ccf_values <- bind_rows(ccf_results) %>%
  mutate(
    Significant = abs(CCF) > Approx_95_Bound
  )

write_csv(
  ccf_values,
  file.path(
    diff_folder,
    "CCF_first_difference_all_values.csv"
  )
)

# Check the results
head(ccf_values)
```
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Folder for saving first-difference CCF plots
diff_plot_folder <- file.path(
  week4_folder,
  "CCF_First_Difference",
  "Plots"
)

dir.create(
  diff_plot_folder,
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

# Prepare readable labels
diff_ccf_plot_data <- ccf_values %>%
  mutate(
    Job_Type = recode(
      Job_Openings,
      "DA"  = "Data Analysis",
      "SW"  = "Software Development",
      "ALL" = "All Job Openings",
      .default = Job_Openings
    ),

    Predictor_Label = case_when(
      Category == "Google Trends" ~ Predictor %>%
        gsub("^GT Job: ", "Job Title: ", .) %>%
        gsub("^GT Skill: ", "Skill: ", .) %>%
        gsub("[_.]", " ", .),

      Category == "Stock Prices" ~ recode(
        Predictor,
        "MSFT"  = "Microsoft",
        "C3AI"  = "C3.ai",
        "NVDA"  = "NVIDIA",
        "GOOGL" = "Alphabet",
        .default = Predictor
      ),

      Category == "CAPEX and PPI" &
        grepl("PCU|PPI", Predictor, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
        "Producer Price Index (PPI)",

      Category == "CAPEX and PPI" &
        grepl("CAPEX", Predictor, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
        "Capital Expenditure (CAPEX)",

      TRUE ~ Predictor
    )
  )

# Create one set of CCF plots for each predictor category
for (category_name in unique(diff_ccf_plot_data$Category)) {

  category_data <- diff_ccf_plot_data %>%
    filter(Category == category_name)

  # Number of facet columns
  facet_columns <- case_when(
    category_name == "Google Trends" ~ 3,
    category_name == "Stock Prices" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ 2
  )

  # Create a separate plot for each job-opening category
  for (job_name in unique(category_data$Job_Type)) {

    plot_data <- category_data %>%
      filter(Job_Type == job_name)

    if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
      next
    }

    confidence_bounds <- plot_data %>%
      distinct(
        Predictor_Label,
        Approx_95_Bound
      )

    diff_ccf_plot <- ggplot(
      plot_data,
      aes(
        x = Lag,
        y = CCF
      )
    ) +

      # Zero-correlation line
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = 0,
        linewidth = 0.45,
        color = "black"
      ) +

      # Approximate 95% confidence limits
      geom_hline(
        data = confidence_bounds,
        aes(yintercept = Approx_95_Bound),
        linetype = "dashed",
        linewidth = 0.5,
        color = "steelblue"
      ) +

      geom_hline(
        data = confidence_bounds,
        aes(yintercept = -Approx_95_Bound),
        linetype = "dashed",
        linewidth = 0.5,
        color = "steelblue"
      ) +

      # CCF stems
      geom_segment(
        aes(
          xend = Lag,
          y = 0,
          yend = CCF
        ),
        linewidth = 0.6,
        color = "gray35"
      ) +

      # Mark lag zero
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = 0,
        linewidth = 0.5,
        color = "black"
      ) +

      facet_wrap(
        ~ Predictor_Label,
        ncol = facet_columns,
        scales = "free_y"
      ) +

      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = seq(
          min(plot_data$Lag, na.rm = TRUE),
          max(plot_data$Lag, na.rm = TRUE),
          by = 10
        )
      ) +

      coord_cartesian(
        ylim = c(-1, 1)
      ) +

      labs(
        title = paste0(
          "First-Difference Cross-Correlation: ",
          job_name
        ),

        subtitle = paste0(
          job_name,
          " versus ",
          category_name,
          "; positive lags indicate that the predictor leads job openings"
        ),

        x = "Lag in days",
        y = "Cross-correlation coefficient",

        caption = paste0(
          "All variables were first-differenced before calculating the CCF. ",
          "Dashed lines show approximate 95% confidence limits."
        )
      ) +

      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(
          face = "bold",
          size = 18
        ),

        plot.subtitle = element_text(
          size = 11,
          color = "gray35",
          margin = margin(b = 10)
        ),

        strip.text = element_text(
          face = "bold",
          size = 10
        ),

        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

        panel.spacing = grid::unit(
          1,
          "lines"
        ),

        plot.caption = element_text(
          hjust = 0,
          face = "italic",
          color = "gray40"
        )
      )

    # Display in the rendered QMD
    print(diff_ccf_plot)

    # Create safe filename
    file_name <- paste0(
      "First_Difference_CCF_",
      gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", job_name),
      "_vs_",
      gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", category_name),
      ".png"
    )

    # Save the plot
    ggsave(
      filename = file.path(
        diff_plot_folder,
        file_name
      ),
      plot = diff_ccf_plot,
      width = 13,
      height = 9,
      dpi = 300,
      bg = "white"
    )
  }
}
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------

capex_ppi_ccf_diff <- ccf_values %>%
  filter(Category == "CAPEX and PPI") %>%
  mutate(
    Job_Type = recode(
      Job_Openings,
      "ALL" = "All Job Openings",
      "DA"  = "Data Analysis",
      "SW"  = "Software Development",
      .default = Job_Openings
    ),

    Indicator = case_when(
      grepl("PCU|PPI", Predictor, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
        "Producer Price Index (PPI)",

      grepl("CAPEX", Predictor, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
        "Capital Expenditure (CAPEX)",

      TRUE ~ Predictor
    ),

    Job_Type = factor(
      Job_Type,
      levels = c(
        "All Job Openings",
        "Data Analysis",
        "Software Development"
      )
    ),

    Indicator = factor(
      Indicator,
      levels = c(
        "Capital Expenditure (CAPEX)",
        "Producer Price Index (PPI)"
      )
    )
  )

# Confidence limits for each panel
capex_ppi_bounds_diff <- capex_ppi_ccf_diff %>%
  distinct(
    Job_Type,
    Indicator,
    Approx_95_Bound
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create the faceted CCF plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

capex_ppi_ccf_diff_plot <- ggplot(
  capex_ppi_ccf_diff,
  aes(
    x = Lag,
    y = CCF
  )
) +

  # Zero-correlation line
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linewidth = 0.4,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  # Approximate 95% confidence limits
  geom_hline(
    data = capex_ppi_bounds_diff,
    aes(yintercept = Approx_95_Bound),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.45,
    color = "steelblue"
  ) +

  geom_hline(
    data = capex_ppi_bounds_diff,
    aes(yintercept = -Approx_95_Bound),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.45,
    color = "steelblue"
  ) +

  # CCF stems
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      xend = Lag,
      y = 0,
      yend = CCF
    ),
    linewidth = 0.55,
    color = "#3B4CC0"
  ) +

  # Mark lag zero
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linewidth = 0.65,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  # Rows = job openings; columns = economic indicators
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(Job_Type),
    cols = vars(Indicator)
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(-30, 30, by = 10)
  ) +

  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(-30, 30),
    ylim = c(-1, 1)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = paste0(
      "Cross-Correlation Between First-Differenced ",
      "Job Openings and Economic Indicators"
    ),

    subtitle = paste0(
      "CCF patterns across lags for daily changes in ",
      "CAPEX and the Producer Price Index"
    ),

    x = "Lag in days",
    y = "Cross-correlation coefficient",

    caption = paste0(
      "All variables were first-differenced before calculating the CCF. ",
      "Dashed lines represent approximate 95% confidence limits. ",
      "Positive lags indicate that changes in the economic indicator ",
      "lead changes in job openings."
    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 12,
      color = "gray35",
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),

    strip.text.x = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 10
    ),

    strip.text.y = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 10
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    panel.spacing = grid::unit(
      0.7,
      "lines"
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    ),

    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      face = "italic",
      size = 9,
      color = "gray35"
    )
  )

capex_ppi_ccf_diff_plot

# Save the plot
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    diff_plot_folder,
    "First_Difference_CCF_Job_Openings_vs_CAPEX_PPI.png"
  ),
  plot = capex_ppi_ccf_diff_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

## ARIMA. model

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

# Number of days to forecast
forecast_horizon <- 30

# Readable names
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "Data Analysis Job Openings",
  SW  = "Software Development Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Fit separate univariate auto.arima models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

arima_models <- lapply(
  names(job_columns),
  function(job_name) {

    column_name <- job_columns[[job_name]]

    # Daily time series with weekly seasonality
    y <- ts(
      na.interp(combined_data[[column_name]]),
      frequency = 7
    )

    auto.arima(
      y,
      seasonal = TRUE,
      stepwise = FALSE,
      approximation = FALSE
    )
  }
)

names(arima_models) <- names(job_columns)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Forecast each series
# ------------------------------------------------------------

arima_forecasts <- lapply(
  arima_models,
  forecast,
  h = forecast_horizon,
  level = c(80, 95)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Prepare historical data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

historical_data <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(job_columns), function(job_name) {

    tibble(
      Date = combined_data$Date,
      Value = combined_data[[job_columns[[job_name]]]],
      Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
    )
  })
) %>%
  drop_na(Value)

# Future dates
future_dates <- seq(
  max(combined_data$Date) + 1,
  by = "day",
  length.out = forecast_horizon
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Prepare forecast results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

forecast_data <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(arima_forecasts), function(job_name) {

    fc <- arima_forecasts[[job_name]]

    tibble(
      Date = future_dates,
      Forecast = as.numeric(fc$mean),
      Lower_80 = as.numeric(fc$lower[, "80%"]),
      Upper_80 = as.numeric(fc$upper[, "80%"]),
      Lower_95 = as.numeric(fc$lower[, "95%"]),
      Upper_95 = as.numeric(fc$upper[, "95%"]),
      Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
    )
  })
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot historical values and forecasts
# ------------------------------------------------------------

arima_forecast_plot <- ggplot() +

  geom_line(
    data = historical_data,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Value
    ),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    color = "#1F5A94"
  ) +

  geom_ribbon(
    data = forecast_data,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      ymin = Lower_95,
      ymax = Upper_95
    ),
    fill = "#9ECAE1",
    alpha = 0.35
  ) +

  geom_ribbon(
    data = forecast_data,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      ymin = Lower_80,
      ymax = Upper_80
    ),
    fill = "#4292C6",
    alpha = 0.40
  ) +

  geom_line(
    data = forecast_data,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Forecast
    ),
    linewidth = 0.9,
    color = "#B2182B"
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = max(combined_data$Date),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    color = "gray35"
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Job_Type ~ .,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Univariate ARIMA Forecasts for Job Openings",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Separate auto.arima models with ",
      forecast_horizon,
      "-day forecasts"
    ),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Job-posting index",
    caption = paste0(
      "Red lines show forecasts. Dark and light shaded regions ",
      "represent 80% and 95% prediction intervals."
    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "gray35"
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      face = "italic"
    )
  )

arima_forecast_plot

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Display selected models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

arima_models$DA
arima_models$SW
arima_models$ALL
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

# Number of observations used for testing
test_horizon <- 30

# Readable category names
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "Data Analysis Job Openings",
  SW  = "Software Development Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

prediction_results <- list()
arima_test_models <- list()

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {

  job_column <- job_columns[[job_name]]

  # Prepare the series
  series_data <- combined_data %>%
    select(
      Date,
      Value = all_of(job_column)
    ) %>%
    arrange(Date)

  # Interpolate missing observations
  full_series <- ts(
    forecast::na.interp(series_data$Value),
    frequency = 7
  )

  # Training and testing data
  train_series <- head(
    full_series,
    -test_horizon
  )

  test_series <- tail(
    full_series,
    test_horizon
  )

  test_dates <- tail(
    series_data$Date,
    test_horizon
  )

  # Fit auto.arima using only the training data
  model <- auto.arima(
    train_series,
    seasonal = TRUE,
    stepwise = FALSE,
    approximation = FALSE
  )

  # Predict the test period
  prediction <- forecast(
    model,
    h = test_horizon,
    level = c(80, 95)
  )

  # Save the model
  arima_test_models[[job_name]] <- model

  # Save actual and predicted values
  prediction_results[[job_name]] <- tibble(
    Date = test_dates,
    Actual = as.numeric(test_series),
    Predicted = as.numeric(prediction$mean),
    Lower_95 = as.numeric(prediction$lower[, "95%"]),
    Upper_95 = as.numeric(prediction$upper[, "95%"]),
    Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
  )
}

# Combine the three results
actual_prediction_data <- bind_rows(
  prediction_results
)

# Plot actual versus predicted values
actual_vs_prediction_plot <- ggplot(
  actual_prediction_data,
  aes(x = Date)
) +

  # 95% prediction interval
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = Lower_95,
      ymax = Upper_95
    ),
    fill = "gray70",
    alpha = 0.35
  ) +

  # Actual values
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Actual,
      color = "Actual"
    ),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = Actual,
      color = "Actual"
    ),
    size = 1.5
  ) +

  # Predicted values
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Predicted,
      color = "Predicted"
    ),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = Predicted,
      color = "Predicted"
    ),
    size = 1.5
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Job_Type ~ .,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actual" = "#1F5A94",
      "Predicted" = "#B2182B"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Actual Versus Predicted Job Openings",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Univariate auto.arima predictions for the final ",
      test_horizon,
      " days"
    ),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Job-posting index",
    color = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Dashed red lines show predictions. ",
      "Shaded areas represent 95% prediction intervals."
    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "gray35"
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      face = "italic"
    )
  )

actual_vs_prediction_plot
```

## Prophet model

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(prophet)

# install.packages("prophet")  # Run once if Prophet is not installed

# Number of final observations used as the test period
test_horizon <- 30

# Readable category names
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "Data Analysis Job Openings",
  SW  = "Software Development Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

prophet_models <- list()
prophet_predictions <- list()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit one Prophet model for each job-opening series
# ------------------------------------------------------------

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {

  job_column <- job_columns[[job_name]]

  # Prophet requires columns named ds and y
  series_data <- combined_data %>%
    transmute(
      ds = as.Date(Date),
      y = as.numeric(.data[[job_column]])
    ) %>%
    arrange(ds) %>%
    filter(!is.na(y))

  # Split into training and testing periods
  train_data <- head(
    series_data,
    -test_horizon
  )

  test_data <- tail(
    series_data,
    test_horizon
  )

  # Fit the Prophet model using training data only
  model <- prophet(
    train_data,
    daily.seasonality = FALSE,
    weekly.seasonality = TRUE,
    yearly.seasonality = TRUE,
    interval.width = 0.95
  )

  # Predict the dates in the test period
  test_forecast <- predict(
    model,
    test_data %>%
      select(ds)
  )

  # Save fitted model
  prophet_models[[job_name]] <- model

  # Save actual and predicted values
  prophet_predictions[[job_name]] <- tibble(
    Date = test_data$ds,
    Actual = test_data$y,
    Predicted = test_forecast$yhat,
    Lower_95 = test_forecast$yhat_lower,
    Upper_95 = test_forecast$yhat_upper,
    Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
  )
}

# Combine results from the three models
prophet_actual_prediction_data <- bind_rows(
  prophet_predictions
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot actual versus predicted values
# ------------------------------------------------------------

prophet_actual_vs_predicted_plot <- ggplot(
  prophet_actual_prediction_data,
  aes(x = Date)
) +

  # 95% prediction interval
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = Lower_95,
      ymax = Upper_95
    ),
    fill = "gray70",
    alpha = 0.35
  ) +

  # Actual values
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Actual,
      color = "Actual"
    ),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = Actual,
      color = "Actual"
    ),
    size = 1.5
  ) +

  # Prophet predictions
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Predicted,
      color = "Prophet Prediction"
    ),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = Predicted,
      color = "Prophet Prediction"
    ),
    size = 1.5
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Job_Type ~ .,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actual" = "#1F5A94",
      "Prophet Prediction" = "#B2182B"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Actual Versus Predicted Job Openings",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Prophet predictions for the final ",
      test_horizon,
      " observations"
    ),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Job-posting index",
    color = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Dashed red lines show Prophet predictions. ",
      "Shaded regions show 95% prediction intervals."
    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "gray35"
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      face = "italic"
    )
  )

prophet_actual_vs_predicted_plot
```
